title: Schema and Item Model Technical Reference
readerIntent: Review schema metadata, extension boundaries, and integration obligations.
owner: Nodics data-model framework and owning business modules
summary: Schema definitions are business contracts; generated runtime models and configured providers implement them without transferring ownership.

sections.heading: Definition and inheritance
items: A schema declares only its owned differences while framework loading merges supported base composition at runtime; do not repeat base inheritance unless the contract requires it explicitly.
Properties define type, cardinality, required, default, constraints, mutability, visibility, masking, ownership, catalog/version behavior, and relationships.
Use stable business codes and descriptions for human identity while provider-generated identifiers remain persistence references.

sections.heading: Relationships and nested work
items: Declare target schema, owning module, cardinality, required behavior, delete semantics, search projection, select-existing, and nested-create policy.
Cross-module relations invoke the target module's model and service APIs with tenant and authorization; they never write another collection directly.
Axis may render generic selection and nested forms, but each target action enforces its own create, read, search, update, field, and ownership rules.

sections.heading: Persistence, search, and publishing
items: Generated item models use database-handler services for authoritative persistence; corresponding search models define provider-neutral query and index projections.
Indexes, uniqueness, transactions, cache invalidation, events, import/export, audit, and search refresh follow owned lifecycle contracts.
Versioning and nPublish are enabled per module/schema configuration; staged and Online remain separate authorities rather than a generic status flag.

sections.heading: Evolution and verification
items: Schema changes assess existing data, defaults, compatibility, indexes, relations, APIs, imports, search mappings, caches, workflows, publication, migration, and rollback.
Test create, read, update, delete, search, required and boundary values, inheritance, field masks, ownership, nested relations, cycles, tenant isolation, concurrency, and provider behavior.
Keep customizable policy in properties.js, remove unused definitions safely, regenerate derived context, and update business and developer documentation with examples.

sections.heading: Review checklist
items: Stable code, owner, description, identity, active state, and base composition.
Property type, required state, default, constraints, mutability, visibility, and masking.
Relationships, cardinality, target owner, nested-create policy, and removal behavior.
Tenant, enterprise, catalog, ownership, group access, and field-level policy.
Indexes, uniqueness, transactions, cache, search, versioning, publishing, audit, events, and workflows.
Runtime governance eligibility and layered customization contract.

sections.heading: Authority boundaries
items: schemas.js owns declarative schema differences; reusable policy values belong in properties.js.
Item models and model-handler services own provider-neutral record interaction.
Database adapters own connection and vendor mapping only.
Search models own query/index behavior, not authoritative persistence.
Axis renders schema metadata and invokes governed APIs; it does not own validation or business rules.
